# A published S2 covering of a real place, with the coordinates it covers.
#
# Provenance: google/s2geometry, src/s2/s2region_coverer_test.cc, TEST
# (JavaCcConsistency, CheckCovering) at lines 534-563.  The test builds a
# polyline through the two published points below, then asks an S2RegionCoverer
# for a covering with the published options and requires exactly the token list
# that follows.  The test exists to pin this implementation against the
# Java/C++ port's answers, which is what makes it an independent oracle rather
# than a self-generated one.
#
#   points (lat_deg, lng_deg), in order:
#     -33.8663457,          151.1960891
#     -33.866094000000004,  151.19517439999998
#
#   options: min_level 0, max_level 22, level_mod 1, max_cells 2147483647
#     (INT_MAX; src/s2/s2region_coverer_test.cc:538-541)
#
# Both points sit inside one of the published cells, because that polyline
# covering covers the whole segment between them at level 22 with no cell-count
# limit.  A zero-radius cap at either coordinate is a region of exactly one
# point, so a covering of it at the same level and with no cell-count limit is
# exactly the single level-22 cell that contains that point -- and that cell is
# one of the tokens published below.  That is the property tests.zig asserts:
# not "the covering is non-empty", but "our coverer, given these coordinates
# and these options, selects a cell from Google's own published list".
#
# Tokens, one per line, in the published order.
